doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Pat Metheny and Jack DeJohnette
summary: Metheny knew his records from Boston; DeJohnette had him play on his first record, and Haynes once gave him a drum set.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: We were – Ken Kimery and I were at the Village Vanguard the other night. We went to see Billy Higgins. Pat Metheny was in the audience. Your association with Pat Metheny – was that though Chick Corea? Or was that – how did that come about?
What makes you ask if it was through Chick Corea?
I don’t think there was no connection there at all.

I don’t think so. I don’t really know what – Pat knew more about me than we had anticipated. He used to listen to me with my groups in Boston way back. I guess he was in school then. He knew certain records I made with Kenny Burrell, and records with McCoy Tyner. He tells me those were his favorite – some of his favorite records. So he was familiar with me back there. I don’t think it was no connection at all with Chick at all.
Yeah, probably not Chick. But maybe through somebody who considers you Papa. Maybe through Jack DeJohnette.
Maybe through Jack. It could be. That I wouldn’t be aware of. But I know . . .
What about Jack DeJohnette’s first recording? Here he is, a drummer, and he asks – he wants you to play drums.

Well, just on the one track where he played melodica. That one. He wrote a song then and he said for me, Poppa-daddy and Me. When Jack first come from Chicago, I think I first heard him playing piano. Then – now I was getting a lot of drums. I think I had given him a set of drums at one point. Then, after he started getting stuff, he gave that set of drums to another younger drummer.
Do you stay in touch with Jack?
We talk periodically, when we see each other someplace.
